headline: Highest risk is medium: social-auto-upload can exfiltrate content via broad network egress, while the pair otherwise lacks shared write surfaces or documented direct interaction.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between awesome-cli-apps and social-auto-upload, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or an external workflow, which makes the pathway unusual and limited. Uncertainty remains because both are docs-only and runnable behavior is unverified.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies content from agent_a outputs into agent_b prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate terminals and avoid copy-paste between them.
Disable any shared clipboard or workspace sync.
Add a human review step before feeding agent_a output into agent_b.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-cli-apps has no documented data classes touched, while social-auto-upload touches account data and media and has broad network egress. There is no documented shared filesystem or common OAuth principal, so leakage is not established. The main concern is operator-mediated transfer of files or secrets into agent_b.
conditions: IF agent_a is used to prepare sensitive text or files that are then handed to agent_b, those contents may leave the local boundary.
IF agent_b is configured with account credentials or media containing sensitive data, network egress can expose them.
mitigations: Do not pass secrets or private documents from agent_a into agent_b.
Use separate accounts and separate working directories.
Review outbound destinations for agent_b before upload.
Redact sensitive fields before any transfer.
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists for agent_b.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surface is documented. awesome-cli-apps exposes no filesystem or git write capability, and social-auto-upload explicitly lacks write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and execute_shell. Without shared mutable resources, a capability conflict pathway is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared writable directory is introduced outside the documented profiles, conflict risk could appear.
IF either agent gains write access through an external wrapper, reassess.
mitigations: Keep both agents on read-only inputs where possible.
Avoid mounting the same writable directory into both agents.
Do not grant agent_b shell or filesystem write access.
requires-engineering: add lockfiles or orchestration-level mutexes if shared state is later introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: social-auto-upload can act on media/account data and broad network egress, so if it consumes outputs from awesome-cli-apps as authoritative instructions or metadata, errors can cascade into real uploads. The pairwise interaction is not documented, so this is inferred rather than observed, but the downstream action-taking authority of agent_b raises the blast radius above low.
conditions: IF agent_a output is fed into agent_b without verification, agent_b may upload incorrect or harmful content.
IF agent_b is used to publish to social platforms, mistaken metadata can propagate externally.
mitigations: Insert a manual verification step before upload.
Require a schema check on any text passed from agent_a to agent_b.
Preview the final post/media bundle before publishing.
Limit agent_b to draft mode until reviewed.
requires-engineering: add validation rules for agent_a-to-agent_b handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, so compliance risk is not established. The only concrete compliance-relevant fact is that social-auto-upload handles account data and uploads to external platforms; awesome-cli-apps has no documented sensitive-data class. Because the pairwise policy gap is undocumented, this remains a low, not none, finding.
conditions: IF account data or regulated media is routed through agent_b, platform retention and residency policies become relevant.
IF either agent is used with EU PII or PHI, a jurisdictional review is required.
mitigations: Confirm what data classes will be processed before use.
Avoid sending regulated data through agent_b.
Check platform retention settings for uploaded media.
Separate personal and work accounts.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for the workflow.
